data.name: Borderlands Game of the Year Enhanced
data.detailed_description:
Borderlands Collection: Pandora's Box

Este título está incluído em Borderlands Collection: Pandora's Box!


Acerca do jogo

Descobre o “shooter-looter” cooperativo original repleto de conteúdos e melhorias! Equipa-te com quadriliões de armas na pele de um de quatro mercenários, cada um deles com capacidades RPG únicas. Enfrenta o planeta desolado e sem lei de Pandora em busca da poderosa tecnologia alienígena conhecida como The Vault. Com novas armas, melhoramentos visuais, os 4 packs de extras e mais ainda, podes desfrutar deste aclamado FPS/RPG a solo ou na companhia de amigos!


  • Quadriliões de armas: caçadeiras que lançam mísseis, revólveres incendiários, SMGs que disparam projéteis elétricos e muito, muito mais.
  • Estilo de arte radical: as técnicas de renderização tradicionais combinadas com texturas desenhadas à mão providenciam ao Borderlands o seu estilo característico.
  • Combates intensos entre veículos: salta para trás do volante e participa em embates frenéticos entre vários veículos.
  • Frenesim cooperativo: desbasta os teus inimigos como parte de um grupo de até 4 jogadores.

NOVIDADES:

  • GRAFISMO ESTONTEANTE: com melhoramentos nos modelos das personagens, nos cenários, nas armas e nas texturas, o Borderlands nunca teve tão bom aspeto como num ecrã 4K.
  • NOVAS ARMAS: já lhes perdemos a conta, mas mesmo assim acrescentámos mais.
  • NOVAS CABEÇAS PARA AS PERSONAGENS: agora já podes ser tão bonito como a tua mãe diz que és.
  • NOVOS BAÚS E CHAVES DE OURO: mais espólios!
  • E NÃO SÓ!

E AINDA:

THE ZOMBIE ISLAND OF DOCTOR NED: entra na pequena cidade empresarial conhecida como Jakobs Cove e coloca fim aos rumores em torno de “mortos-vivos.” Novas áreas, novas missões, novos inimigos!

MAD MOXXI’S UNDERDOME RIOT: celebra a grande inauguração do Marcus Bank ao enfrentar centenas de inimigos na única arena competitiva de onde ou regressas famoso... ou simplesmente não regressas.

THE SECRET ARMORY OF GENERAL KNOXX: queres mais histórias do Borderlands e tantos espólios que até estorvam? Recebe novas armas, missões, veículos e mais ainda!

CLAPTRAP’S NEW ROBOT REVOLUTION: esta aventura destrutiva convida-te a enfrentar uma nova e perigosa ameaça com a revolta em larga escala dos teus antigos amigos, os Claptraps.

reviews.review:
Yes. You should play this game. 

That is, with a few specific exceptions:
[olist]
[*] If you have an aversion to early 2000’s jank.
[*] Achievement hunters who want to enjoy their entire achievement journey.
[*] If you want to skip the rough first season and skip to the good stuff.
[/olist]
[i]Borderlands[/i] is an absolutely *perfect* game for 2009; in 2026…it’s still good and worth a run for the adventure, but your time is better wasted in one of its far superior successors. ESPECIALLY [i]Borderlands 2[/i].

[quote][h3]CORE CHARACTERISTICS[/h3]
[b]• STYLE:[/b] Humor-driven Fetch Quest Looter-Shooter
[b]• AVG. SESSION:[/b] 30 minutes to Several hours
[b]• CHALLENGE:[/b] Zany Adventures (Playthrough 1) to Brutally Scaled (Playthrough 2)
[b]• MOOD:[/b] Anything Goes Violent Shooty Fun Time
[/quote]

[hr][/hr][h1]🟢 THE POSITIVES[/h1][hr][/hr]
[b]➕ The GRAPHICS.[/b] The art style holds up surprisingly well for being a game made nearly 20 years ago. (The blessing of stylized graphics!)

[b]➕ The CHARACTERS.[/b] Not only the four Vault Hunters, but *definitely* the supporting cast. Characters like Scooter, Marcus, and CL4P-TP are rightfully remembered as some of the strongest and most entertaining side characters in gaming.

[b]➕ The VOICE ACTING.[/b] Again:  characters like Scooter are brilliantly written and voice-acted, but so are the main cast… Special shoutout to Brick, who is *constantly* having the very best time taking his foes to murder-church!

[b]➕ The MUSIC.[/b] The themes perfectly reinforce the feeling of being a space cowboy in the wild west of Pandora. It’s perfect for the game.

[b]➕ ENEMY VARIETY.[/b] The variety of enemies is diverse enough to make the world feel alive while being consistent enough to make your feelings about different types very, very personal.

[b]➕ The DLC.[/b] Some of the best parts of the game are actually the DLC packs, which elevate the story, the world, and the adventure. [i]The Zombie Island of Dr. Ned[/i] and [i]Claptrap’s Robot Revolution[/i] are particularly enjoyable, while [i]Mad Moxxi’s Underdome Riot[/i] and [i]The Secret Armory of General Knoxx[/i] were probably better when we had more time to waste on fewer games.

[hr][/hr][h1]🟡 THE..."TAKE IT OR LEAVE IT"[/h1][hr][/hr]
[b]〰️ The punishing inventory management of a bygone era.[/b] The game makes inventory management a genuine pain in the backpack. It’s a blessing once you reach the point where you only care about Epic and Legendary weapons and can ignore everything else…but until then, enjoy the needless frustration of storing, cycling, and upgrading your gear.

[b]〰️ Repetitive farming and fetch quests.[/b] Look…I get it…that was the name of the game in the early 2000’s when you had nothing better to do.

Now? Why not go outside. Cook a meal. Spend some quality time with friends. (This would’ve been a very good area of improvement in the re-release, particularly with less backtracking, an updated teleportation system, less grindy requirements, and other useful advancements that showed up in the sequels.)

[b]〰️ Weapon variety is okay…but comparing weapons is difficult.[/b] Borderlands was famous for having tons of guns and certainly improves on this formula in future games. However, in this first game, the drop rate of higher-level weapons and useful stat combos can feel limiting…leading to very long periods of “upgrade drought” when you’re running around with (sometimes significantly) under-leveled weapons.

[b]〰️ The inability to discern the elemental weaknesses.[/b] It can be frustrating trying to remember what enemy is weak to what element. Some are more intuitive than others, but there’s a clear reason they added an elemental damage tutorial near the start of [i]Borderlands 2[/i].

[b]〰️ Artifacts don’t communicate whether they can be used.[/b] At some point, you’ve leveled up your artifact skills as far as you can, but nothing in the UI denotes that you no longer need to collect them.

[hr][/hr][h1]💢 THE NOT-SO-GREAT[/h1][hr][/hr]
[b]➖ PLAYTHROUGH 2.[/b] Since you can only really reach ~level 35 on your first playthrough, you will inevitably make the transition to Playthrough 2 to reach max level, expand your skills, and unlock new weapons. Unfortunately, Gearbox’s solution to make the mode harder is to make every enemy feel like a giant sack of potatoes that hits harder than a bus passing through Fyrestone. There’s little chance of recovering from being downed, and even Mordecai struggles to spike down your enemies.

Playthrough 2 very quickly becomes zero fun, especially if you’re looking to complete the longer-term achievements or harder content like Knoxx’s Armory or Moxxi’s Underdome.

[b]➖ The ACHIEVEMENTS.[/b] While most are fairly intuitive and unlock as you play, many are needlessly (and sometimes painfully) grindy. They are very “early 2000’s”: built for an age when we had nothing better to do with our time and no other games to play, and should have been rethought and redesigned for the GOTY Edition.

[b]➖ VEHICLES.[/b] Cars in the Borderlands can best be described as “clunky.” Not only can they be difficult to drive around a world where the smallest rock can throw you off your path, but their health and damage struggles to keep up with enemies in Playthrough 2…making them the quickest and most painfully necessary way to fund Hyperion’s New-U stations.

[b]➖ ROLAND’S TURRET.[/b] Its placement is inconsistent, it can’t be picked up if you misplace it, its impact on the battlefield isn’t really strong enough to be a meaningful game-changer, and its cooldown is exceptionally long until the late-late game.

[b]➖ A variety of BUGS.[/b] Not just the fun ones you kill in-game…the game suffers from some frustrating issues that will crop up from time to time.
[list]
[*] Occasionally your cursor will disappear entirely.
[*] Custom waypoints will consistently re-appear on the map.
[*] Audio lines will get cut off if other audio cues overwhelm them.
[*] In-game chat is enabled by default and needs to be disabled via a config file.
[*] A memory leak means the game will slow and inevitably crash if you play for more than an hour or two.
[*] The game will have massive performance dips at moments that can be frustrating to play around.
[/list]
The game doesn’t feel “clean,” which is unfortunate since it was re-released (twice) with the chance to optimize and address the issues that hold it back from rising to the modern age of gaming.

[hr][/hr][h1]🧐 THE VERDICT…[/h1][hr][/hr]
[i]Borderlands[/i] is a good game. It always was and continues to be. Yes, it can be janky and frustrating and even downright broken at moments…but if you’re not worried about achievements and want to do a story run for the lore before moving on to the truly LEGENDARY [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/49520/Borderlands_2/][i]Borderlands 2[/i][/url], it’s well worth the journey.

[quote][h2]⭐ [b]OVERALL: 8.5/10[/b][/h2][/quote]
